promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: The use of authority in daily life

questions.q: Which text is regarded as the holy book of Islam?
questions.explain: The Qur'an is the central sacred text of Islam, believed by Muslims to be the word of God.

questions.q: The Christian Bible is divided into which two main sections?
questions.explain: The Christian Bible comprises the Old Testament and the New Testament.

questions.q: In Judaism, the Torah refers to which part of scripture?
options: The first five books of the Tenakh
The writings of the prophets alone
questions.explain: The Torah is the first five books of the Tenakh, traditionally associated with Moses.

questions.q: What is the principal sacred scripture of Sikhism?
questions.explain: The Guru Granth Sahib is the central scripture of Sikhism.

questions.q: By what name was the Buddha known before his enlightenment?
questions.explain: The Buddha was born Siddhartha Gautama before achieving enlightenment.

questions.q: Who was the first of the Sikh Gurus?
questions.explain: Guru Nanak was the founder of Sikhism and the first of the Gurus.

questions.q: Who is the spiritual leader of the Roman Catholic Church?
questions.explain: The Pope is the head of the Roman Catholic Church, regarded as the successor of St Peter.

questions.q: The Buddhist scripture known as the Tripitaka takes its name from a phrase meaning what?
questions.explain: Tripitaka means 'Three Baskets', referring to its three collections of teachings.

questions.q: According to Islamic belief, the Qur'an was revealed to Muhammad through which angel?
questions.explain: Muslims believe the angel Jibril (Gabriel) transmitted God's revelations to Muhammad.

questions.q: Why do Sikhs treat the Guru Granth Sahib as a living Guru?
options: Guru Gobind Singh declared it the final and eternal Guru
It was written by God directly
It contains only the words of Guru Nanak
It replaced the need for worship
questions.explain: Guru Gobind Singh ended the line of human Gurus and installed the scripture as the eternal Guru.

questions.q: The Bhagavad Gita records a conversation between which two figures?
questions.explain: The Bhagavad Gita presents a dialogue between the warrior Arjuna and Krishna on duty and devotion.

questions.q: Muslims describe Muhammad as the 'Seal of the Prophets' because he is believed to be what?
options: The final prophet sent by God
questions.explain: The title means Muhammad is regarded as the last in the line of prophets.

questions.q: What is the main role of an imam in a Sunni mosque?
options: To lead the congregation in prayer
To forgive sins on God's behalf
questions.explain: In Sunni Islam the imam chiefly leads communal prayer and may offer teaching.

questions.q: In Judaism, a rabbi is best described as which of the following?
options: A teacher of the Torah and Jewish law
A monk who lives in isolation
questions.explain: A rabbi is a trained teacher and interpreter of the Torah and Jewish law.

questions.q: How many human Gurus does the Sikh tradition recognise?
questions.explain: Sikhism recognises ten human Gurus, from Guru Nanak to Guru Gobind Singh.

questions.q: Sharia in Islam is best understood as which of the following?
options: A body of law and guidance shaping how Muslims should live
questions.explain: Sharia provides religious law and moral guidance for everyday Muslim life.

questions.q: A Muslim facing a difficult moral decision wishes to follow religious authority. Which sources would she most likely turn to first?
options: The Qur'an and the Sunnah of the Prophet
questions.explain: Muslims look primarily to the Qur'an and the example of Muhammad (Sunnah) for guidance.

questions.q: A Jewish family keeps kosher food laws in daily life. On which source of authority are these laws principally based?
options: The Torah and its interpretation in Jewish law
questions.explain: Kosher dietary rules derive from the Torah and its interpretation within Jewish law.

questions.q: A Christian is unsure how to act and prays for inner moral guidance about right and wrong. Which source of authority is she chiefly relying on?
questions.explain: Many Christians regard the conscience as an inner, God-given source of moral authority.

questions.q: During worship in the gurdwara, Sikhs seek guidance by reading from which source of authority?
questions.explain: Sikh worship centres on readings from the Guru Granth Sahib, treated as the living Guru.

specSource: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Religious Studies (4RS1) specification; Sources of Wisdom & Authority
